etymologies.etymologyHTML: American English, super- +‎ market, 1933.

definitions.definition: A large self-service store that sells groceries and, usually, medications, household goods, and/or clothing.
(figurative) A one-stop shop; a place offering a range of products or services.

quote.citation: 2011, Faith Glasgow, Personal Finance and Investing All-in-One For Dummies:
quote.text: If you know what you want by filtering down the 1,600 or so trusts to a short list and then studying the information on each via online sources, then you can buy your trust and get all or nearly all of the commission back into your bank account via an Internet investment supermarket. Here, you select your fund, decide whether you want it as an Individual Savings Account (ISA), and pay for it with a credit card.

quote.citation: 2024 February 20, Fiona Vera-Gray, quoting Almina, “‘Everything is hairless’: what 100 women taught me about porn and body confidence”, in The Guardian‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: Almina grew up in the age of the internet and the infinite supermarket of pornography it provides.
